messages:
morgan: Quick q — can someone confirm precedence for flag overrides? I thought order is org -> project -> route -> model, but hitting a weird case: project disables a flag and we want to enable it only for a canary on /api/generate. Does route-level override win?

alex: Yep that's the intended order: org -> project -> route -> model. So route can enable when project disabled. Caveat: org-level immutable flags or denylists can block route overrides (those are enforced as higher priority).

jamie: To add: model-level overrides only apply when the request is model-scoped. If a route is 'model-agnostic' then model override won't be considered. Example config:
```
flag:
  org: enabled
  project: disabled
  route: enabled  # canary: 5% users
  model: disabled
```
In the example route wins for matching traffic and the 5% canary will observe enabled behavior.

sasha: Edge case: projects can set a denylist of routes that must inherit project/org settings (immutable). We added server-side validation but the db still has older rows that bypass it — planning PR to backfill + enforce on write.

samir: FYI on the rollout UI: we compute the effective state in the frontend using the same precedence algo (org -> project -> route -> model) and show an "effective state" badge per-route. If an override is in conflict we surface a warning and the UI suggests admin contact. Also tagged telemetry events with `flag.override` so we can see rate of route-level overrides.

deploy-bot: deploy: flag-service v3.14.2 deployed to staging @eng-platform — includes immutable-flag validation and the telemetry tag.

morgan: Thanks — can someone drop a 1-line explanation + a tiny example I can paste into the release notes for product owners?

alex: I'll draft one in a few.

jamie: One-liner draft: 'Flag resolution precedence is org > project > route > model; route-level canary overrides project-level settings unless the flag is marked immutable by org policies.'

morgan: :thumbsup: perfect.

sasha: Opened PR #789 to enforce denylist at write-time and backfill bad rows. @alex please review when you have a sec.

alex: On it, added a couple inline comments. Should be quick.

morgan: Great — once PR is merged can we get a short changelog note that includes the exact precedence rule + pointer to the rollout UI? I'll file the release note.

jamie: Will add a small docs blurb under 'feature flags -> scope & precedence' after PR is merged.
